items.recapEn: At Hara, Fuji finally appeared, huge above the rice fields in a clear dawn. Hana ran to see it before breakfast; a blue-grey cat on a stone was watching it too. Ken admitted he had climbed it once at nineteen and never would again; the innkeeper Suzuki-san had climbed it eleven times. Hana wrote: I have not climbed it. Yet?

items.recapEn: At breakfast Ken tells Hana to eat before looking at Fuji. Suzuki-san has climbed it eleven times and says the mountain is kind; Ken climbed it once at nineteen, cold and sleepy, and never again. Hana insists the cat in the fields is Ao; Ken says a cat does not walk here from Oiso. They leave at seven.

comprehension.q: What is the weather like in Hara on July 17?

items.recapEn: Hana's postcard home from Hara, with Fuji on the front: a clear July morning, a run to the rice fields before breakfast, packs after eating, Ken drinking coffee while watching the mountain, snow still on the summit. She has never climbed Fuji; Ken has once, the innkeeper eleven times. This year she is only looking.
